chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the heat and the cold, from what do they emanate?

He said to me, 'O Abu Ayyub! Indeed, Mars is a hot planet and Saturn is a cold planet. So when Mars begins to rise, Saturn goes lower, and that is in the spring. So they do not cease being like that; every time Mars rises a degree, Saturn falls a degree for three months, until Mars ends in its height and Saturn ends in its decline, so Mars becomes clear/dominant, and therefore the heat intensifies.'

So when it is at the end of summer and the beginning of autumn, Saturn begins to rise and Mars begins to decline. So they do not cease being like that; every time Saturn rises a degree, Mars falls a degree, until Mars ends in its decline and Saturn ends in its height, so Saturn becomes clear/dominant, and that is at the beginning of winter and the end of autumn, and therefore the cold intensifies.

And every time this one rises, that one falls, and every time that one falls, this one rises. So if there is a cold day in the summer, the action in that is due to the Moon, and if there is a hot day in the winter, the action in that is due to the Sun.
This is the ordinance of the Mighty, the Knowing, and I am the servant of the Lord of the Worlds.'
ai.seo_question: What are the celestial causes of heat and cold according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the celestial mechanics behind seasonal variations, attributing the primary cycles of heat and cold to the inverse orbital movements of Mars (hot) and Saturn (cold). He further distinguishes anomalous weather patterns, such as summer cold snaps or winter heatwaves, by assigning their influence to the Moon and the Sun respectively, thereby integrating planetary astronomy with divine decree (Qadr). This narration reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of harmonizing observed natural phenomena with theological principles, emphasizing that while celestial bodies act as instruments, ultimate control rests with Allah.

en.hubeali: H 14922 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik Bin Atiyya, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said:
I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the heat and the cold, from what do they emanate?’

O Abu Ayyub! Mars is a hot planet and Saturn is a cold planet. So if Mars begins to rise, the Saturn goes lower, and that is in the spring. So they do not stop being like that. Every time Mars rises a level, Saturn falls for three months until the Mars ends up high and Saturn ends up in the decline. 
For the Mars that is its hottest time.

So when it is at the end of the summer and the beginning of the autumn, Saturn begins to ascend and the Mars begins to descend. So these two do not stop being like that. Every time Saturn rises a level, Mars declines a level, and that is at the beginning of the winter and at the end of the summer. So that is its coldest time.

Every time this one rises, this one comes down, and every time this one comes down, this one rises. So if there is a cold day in the summer, so that is the action of the Moon, and if there is a hot day in the winter, so that action is due to the Sun.
“[36:38] that is the ordinance of the Mighty, the Knowing” and Iasws am the servant of the Lordazwj of the Worlds’.
en.sarwar: 475. A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al-Qaddaah, who has narrated the following:
Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said that the Rasool Allah (saww) said: ‘O Ali (a.s.)!

The one who loves you (a.s.), then dies, so he has died. And the one who loves you (a.s.) and has not died yet, so he is awaiting. And the sun does not rise nor sets except that it comes to him with sustenance and the faith’.
